newsitem.title: USA: Hormel in venture with Polish meat firm.
newsitem.headline: Hormel in venture with Polish meat firm.

text.p: Hormel Foods Corp said Monday it entered into a joint venture with Pozmeat SA, a leading Polish manufacturer of sausage, bacon and other perishable and canned meats.
The company said the alliance is the first eastern European investment for its Hormel Foods International Corp subsidiary.
Through the alliance, Hormel branded products will be introduced into Poland, allowing it to expand distribution and strengthen its brand name overseas.
Hormel said it will work with Pozmeat to make and market kielbasa, bologna, ham, bacon and other meat products marketed under the Pozmeat, Krakus, Atalanta, Yano and PEK brands.

Pozmeat, located in a large hog-growing area in Poland, has a broad distribution network, an extensive range of products and an ability to develop and market new products, said V. Allan Krejci, director of public relations for Hormel.

"(Hormel Foods International), in turn, can provide the management expertise, marketing experience and product technology to position Pozmeat as a top European brand while benefiting from this association to introduce and market Hormel Foods product internationally," he added.

Separately, Hormel announced that Robert Wells, vice president of pork, provisions and refineries, will retire December 6. Don Pohlman, vice president of sales for the foodservice group, will retire December 20.
With Wells' retirement, his pork procurement, refinery and feed sales responsibilities are being assigned to and shared by other members of the operations group.
Steven Binder, currently southeast regional sales manager and corporate national accounts manager for foodservice, will replace Pohlman.
